# Database Browser & Custom Fields {#sec-tech-browser}

This chapter covers two of the five Database sub-app panels (@sec-arch-subapp):
`app/view/database_browser.R` (Browse Entries) and `app/view/database_custom.R`
(Custom Variables). The Import/Export panels are @sec-tech-interop and the cgMLST
Overview panel is @sec-tech-schemes-inspect.

## Browse Entries {#sec-tech-browser-browse}

`database_browser.R` shows the isolate table: the `metadata` columns, with the
classical-MLST, AMR and custom-variable columns merged in read-only at display
time (@sec-db-companions). It is the one place metadata *values* are edited, and
it returns a `pending` reactive so `main.R` can warn before a reload would
discard unsaved edits (@sec-arch-signals).

Edits are written as a tidy, one-row-per-changed-cell set — the same shape the
custom-value writer uses — inside a transaction:

```{.r filename="app/logic/database_functions.R"}
#' Deliberately mirrors `save_custom_values()`'s shape: a tidy one-row-per-cell
#' [edit set].
save_metadata_table <- function(db_path, edits) { ... }
```

::: {.callout-important title="The edit grid treats a revision bump as 'stale', not 'reload'"}
Most modules re-query when the revision bus advances. Browse Entries is the
deliberate exception: because it may hold unsaved edits, a bump is treated as a
*staleness marker* rather than a cue to reload over the user's work — the user
asking for a reload is the explicit consent that discards it (@sec-arch-signals).
Any new control in this panel must respect that: never re-render the grid from a
bus bump alone.
:::

Deleting isolates is transactional and offers to keep or drop the now-orphaned
allele sequences:

```{.r filename="app/logic/database_functions.R"}
#' Runs within a transaction to guarantee atomic updates.
remove_isolates <- function(db_path, isolates, keep_alleles = TRUE) { ... }
```

## Custom fields {#sec-tech-browser-custom}

`app/view/database_custom.R`, backed by `app/logic/custom_fields.R`, defines
user-typed fields and their per-isolate values. This is the **only** place custom
values are written; every other view merges them in read-only.

Two tables hold this, both living inside the loaded `.db` (prefixed
`phylotrace_`, so they travel with the file), with values stored **long**:

```{.r filename="app/logic/custom_fields.R"}
"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phylotrace_custom_fields (
   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
   type TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT, levels TEXT, position INTEGER,
   created TEXT NOT NULL, modified TEXT NOT NULL )",
"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phylotrace_custom_values (
   field_id INTEGER NOT NULL, isolate TEXT NOT NULL, value TEXT,
   PRIMARY KEY (field_id, isolate) )"
```

Storing values long rather than one column per variable means renaming a variable
is a single `UPDATE` with no schema change, and pivoting long→wide at display
time is the same pattern the classical-MLST and AMR readers use
(@sec-db-companions). Every value is stored as TEXT in a canonical form (ISO
date, `yes`/`no`, the number as written).

### Typing and validation {#sec-tech-browser-types}

- `create_custom_field()` / `update_custom_field()` / `delete_custom_field()`
  manage definitions; deletion cascades to values in one transaction.
- `validate_custom_name()` rejects reserved prefixes, invalid syntax and
  collisions (custom columns carry a `CUSTOM_COL_PREFIX`, `custom_col()`).
- `coerce_custom_value()` canonicalizes each entered value to its type — a date,
  a yes/no, a number, or one of a categorical field's declared levels
  (`field_levels()`, `encode_levels()`).
- `load_custom_values()` / `append_custom()` pivot the long store to wide and join
  it onto a metadata frame for display.

The declared types are the vocabulary the visualization layer reads to decide how
a variable may be mapped: `app/logic/field_types.R` supplies the type of any
column (fixed, derived or custom), and `app/logic/field_profile.R` profiles a
column's cardinality and coverage — the input the mapping engine ranks aesthetics
from (@sec-tech-viz-mapping).

## Chapter summary

- `database_browser.R` edits metadata values transactionally, merges MLST/AMR/
  custom columns read-only, and guards unsaved edits against reloads.
- `custom_fields.R` stores user-defined typed fields long in two `phylotrace_*`
  tables, so a rename is an `UPDATE` and the fields travel with the file.
- Values are validated and canonicalized on write; the declared type drives what
  the mapping engine will do with the variable.
